reconstruction_summary: V1 = (v/L)*tan(delta) with L=2.984 m (MACH_E wheelbase from out/meta.json) minus a per-segment straight-line bias (mean residual on rows where |delta_road_rad|<0.01, requires >5 such rows else bias=0); reconstructed directly from REPORT.md + out/run_ladder.py — no model coefficients needed beyond the constant L.
notes: Baseline recomputed from sim.csv yaw_rate_pred_rads matches the canonical baseline to <1e-12 rad/s (0.014740020893 vs 0.014740020893). Per-segment straight-line bias is computed on each canonical segment's own rows where |delta_road_rad|<0.01 (no cross-segment leakage by construction); 24 of 545 segments had no post-filter rows and contributed nothing. Agent trained on a 20-segment Mach-E stride with MACH_E parameters; their 'favourite' V1 is a single model with a single wheelbase L=2.984 m. Re-applying that same model to all 545 Ford segments uses L=2.984 for both Mach-E and the F-150 Lightning (true L≈3.696 m), so the F-150 half is scored with a mismatched wheelbase — this is faithful to what the agent shipped and is the apples-to-apples canonical comparison.
